label: Person
name: Adrian Hołownia
summary:
Adrian Hołownia (b. 1970) is a Polish Catholic bishop who serves as auxiliary bishop of the Archdiocese of Gdańsk, one of Poland's most historically significant sees, deeply associated with the Solidarity movement and the Gdańsk Shipyard's role in the fall of communism. Ordained a priest of the Gdańsk archdiocese, he was consecrated auxiliary bishop as the diocese engaged the challenges of postcommunist Polish society.

Gdańsk carries exceptional symbolic weight in Polish national and Catholic consciousness: it was the birthplace of the Solidarity trade union in 1980 and the city where the confluence of Catholic faith, Polish nationalism, and worker solidarity helped bring down communism. Hołownia's ministry in this context requires both pastoral care for a modern Baltic city and stewardship of an extraordinary historical memory.

As auxiliary bishop, his primary responsibilities involve supporting the archbishop in diocesan administration, episcopal visitations, and the coordination of pastoral programmes. His ministry reflects the Polish Church's ongoing challenge of sustaining its post-Solidarity moral authority in a secular, democratic Poland where many younger citizens regard the Church's public role with increasing ambivalence.
